headline: Growth accelerates everywhere as margins hit a record high
summary_short: Ingram Micro's net sales rose 13.6% y/y to $14.53B, up across all four geographic segments, while operating margin expanded 50bp to 1.62% on the absence of last year's held-for-sale write-downs. Diluted EPS was $0.48, versus $0.42 last quarter and $0.16 a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue growth was broad-based: Client & Endpoint Solutions +13%, Advanced Solutions +14% and Cloud +47% globally, partly offset by an 8% Other-services decline and an 11-point drag from the 2025 CloudBlue divestiture. Gross margin ticked up 4bp as the prior year's write-down rolled off, offset by a mix shift toward lower-margin AI-infrastructure hardware. SG&A fell 52bp of sales on automation efficiencies, lifting operating margin to 1.62% from 1.12%. Net income nearly quadrupled on the operating gain, a lower tax rate and a smaller FX loss. Cash fell to $809.0M from $856.7M a year ago as a $1.1B inventory build used $1.51B of operating cash. The board declared a $0.086/share Q3 dividend post-quarter; the filing gives no forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: Growth was broad-based across all four segments, led by Cloud-based Solutions (+47%) and Advanced Solutions (+14%); Other services fell 8% and the 2025 CloudBlue divestiture cut 11 points off Cloud growth.
Margin rose 4bp as the prior year's $10.5M held-for-sale inventory write-down rolled off, partly offset by a mix shift toward lower-margin AI-infrastructure hardware.
Margin expanded 50bp on SG&A leverage from automation/Xvantage efficiencies and the absence of last year's $43.2M CloudBlue and non-core write-down, despite higher bad-debt and restructuring costs.
